seal.statement: The production admin CDC surface owns exactly one live SystemTableCache notification subscription: construction and repeated same-cache binding never duplicate delivery, cache handoff prevents the retired cache from delivering while the replacement remains live, shutdown detaches delivery, and the unchanged release-blocking admin CDC integration passes repeatedly under the release environment without timeout or listener leakage; cache mutation, tombstone fencing, CDC operation payloads, and non-admin subscribers remain unchanged.

text: Release workflow 34444694916 measured one isolated repeated failure: test/integration/admin-cdc-propagation.integration.test.js missed the third subtest INSERT event in both the full integration batch and its automatic standalone retry, while cdc-propagation and cdc-subscription-catchup integrations passed. The exact release environment then passed this file locally five consecutive times. This rules out a simple deterministic cache-mutation failure and keeps both persistent-runner lifecycle pressure and admin subscription ownership in the proof boundary; timeout or one-assertion tuning is ruled out.

Added a real SystemTableCache/AdminWebSocketAPI owner-lifecycle witness before changing production code. On sealed HEAD it fails deterministically: same-cache rebinding grows listeners 1->3, old cache remains live after handoff, all three cache-backed child owners retain the old cache, shutdown retains the listener and delivers post-shutdown events. Command: node scripts/run-test-files.js --jobs=1 test/admin/admin-websocket-api-shutdown-state.test.js (23 assertions, 10 failures).

The canonical-fixture stress reproduced the exact third-subtest miss on repetition 3, followed by a standalone retry pass. Root cause is now deterministic: bootstrap can complete a nodes-table authoritative observation before the test's direct INSERT; SystemTableCache correctly fences an absent-key write that has no causal timestamp at or after that observation. One-line production-cache probe measured unversionedPresent=false and the same INSERT with updated_at=observedAt+1 as versionedPresent=true. The first subtest already supplied timestamps; the third did not. Therefore the release blocker is a scenario-contract violation exposed by convergence timing, not notification latency. The fixture must author monotonically versioned CDC rows and keep tombstone/authoritative-absence fencing unchanged.

Implemented the bounded systemic repair: AdminWebSocketAPI now owns a stable Set-idempotent cache listener, detaches before cache handoff and shutdown, propagates the replacement cache to its control/preflight/discovery child owners, and rebinds on restart. The integration now uses the canonical isolated-storage/port/registry fixture, has no forced process exit, authors INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE timestamps monotonically after the cache's authoritative observation boundary, and asserts mutation revision before delivery. The release-environment integration passed 10/10 consecutive primary runs with retry disabled (290 assertions, zero failures).

Candidate self-check evidence before independent review: release-environment admin CDC strict stress passed 10/10 with retries disabled (290 assertions); focused owner/cache/CDC cone passed 444/444; widened change selection ran 136/136 files with no TAP failures; full npm run test:static passed (unused exports 1438/1438, cycles 0/0, source duplication 57/57 and 1845/1845 lines, test duplication 793/793 and 30519/30519 lines, cyclomatic 1822/1822, cognitive 161/161, file-size 27/27 source and 21/21 test, all architecture/grammar/guideline/shard/docs/lint gates green). Scoped constructor complexity remained exactly 35 before and after. No baseline or budget changed.

REJECT: sequential listener ownership and integration causal fixture are correct, but cache handoff bypasses AdminServiceDiscovery cache-bound repair/backoff lifecycle state, shutdown can race a replacement subscription, initialize can return during shutdown and leave the API stopped, and the AdminWebSocketAPI-SystemTableCache interaction lacks a named impact contract and concurrent witnesses. Evidence: verifier probes f5775f0 (child state reuse), a52fb5d (handoff/shutdown race), 5fca7fd (restart/shutdown race), 30ad0cf (proof selection); fresh cache semantics 375/375 and focused sequential lifecycle 52/52 passed.

Added deterministic owner-boundary witnesses before the second production repair: a deferred Fastify close proves cache handoff during shutdown re-subscribes and strands the replacement listener; initialize during the same close resolves early and leaves Admin stopped; a deferred authoritative discovery read proves handoff preserves the old mutation target, publishes old-owner success, and reuses it. Implemented the verifier-rejected owner boundary as one systemic transition: Admin lifecycle calls now serialize on one promise lane with explicit created/starting/running/stopping/stopped state; shutdown fences subscription synchronously and detaches on every exit; cache handoff transitions coherent read/mutation pairs through typed child setters. AdminServiceDiscovery increments a cache-owner generation, clears success/failure/probe state, captures immutable owner pairs for reconciliation, revalidates after authoritative reads and reconcile awaits, and identity-guards old promise cleanup. Added the named admin-cache-owner-lifecycle impact contract and coupled notification/repair endpoints. Finalized the terminal candidate after static-policy feedback: cacheMutationTarget option detection now uses a named literal owner, and initialization/shutdown cleanup catches emit typed Admin diagnostics instead of becoming silent branches. Re-ran focused lifecycle/repair/cache proof (458/458), full 436-file impact-selected proof (18,636 assertions), exact release integration stress 10/10 with retries disabled, and the complete npm run test:static chain. The setChildCacheOwner compatibility fallback can bypass the required typed child transition. APPROVE: no blocking findings remain. Fresh independent probes proved rejected retired control and discovery attempts return the new owner after exactly two attempts; current-owner errors propagate unchanged after one attempt; mixed rejected/fulfilled churn throws the canonical repeated-owner error after two attempts. Protected cone passed 970/970, impact registry passed with 19 contracts, 10 coupled pairs and digest 97cc5d7924cfc89c679661341d890867311af6471f354fa93f24e558ed49b888, Quest probe measured metric 0 done=true, fast-static and git diff --check passed. Altitude check after 11 measured attempts: the investigation converged from an apparent notification miss to two owner-boundary contracts. First, authoritative-absence fencing is correct and scenario authors must provide monotonic causal CDC timestamps. Second, every asynchronous Admin operation must remain bound to one typed read/mutation cache-owner generation across both fulfillment and rejection, with retired work discarded, current errors preserved, and repeated churn bounded. Those contracts are now centralized, registered as a protected interaction, retained by deterministic red-first witnesses, and independently approved. No cache/CDC core semantic, timeout, retry, cadence, runner, or ratchet change was needed.

The Quest remains at the correct altitude and can succeed here: the apparent notification miss reduced to the producer/cache causal contract plus the shared Admin cache-owner generation contract, not a lower local timeout or a broader cache rewrite. Both owner-boundary contracts are now centralized, protected, red-first witnessed, and independently approved. No cache/CDC semantic, timeout, retry, cadence, runner, or ratchet change is warranted; proceed to landing.
